utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Good afternoon, doctor. Could I remind you that the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon. Could we please display again 65 ter 993. This is also tab 3 of the binders. With the usher's assistance, could we please give the doctor his binder from yesterday. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: This is at tab 3 of the binders. Dr. Jakovski, yesterday we spoke briefly about this document that's being displayed on the screen in front of you. You indicated that the markings on this sketch were written by you and are -- refer to basically injuries and their dimensions that were noted on Atulla Qaili's body at the time of autopsy. Could I ask you whether all of these injuries and their dimensions were also noted in your final autopsy section protocol that you prepared for Mr. Qaili as well?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the changes that are marked on this sketch are described in detail in the section protocol in the sense of the colour, shape, dimension, position.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could we turn, please, to page 2 of this document. Doctor, the handwriting that is on this particular page, is this also your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could you please, so that we can have a translation of this, if you could read, please, what you have written on this particular page in the Macedonian language. That way, we can get a translation of this particular page.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read what is written here on that second page?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes, please, so we can have a translation of this for the record.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forehead bilateral haematoma, on the rear part of the head-- this is a poor copy. I can't read it. It only says on the -- in the face that there is a haematoma. Subdural on the forehead basal, on the back of the head, three centimetres, ribs a left side from the 2nd to the 9th from the parasternal to the median line. From the second, and I can't see then what's written in the copy. From the middle collar-bone to the scapular and 7th in the subscapular area. This is located on the ribs or in the chest. Then it is written the brain, left, from -- on the forehead and the back of the head, on the exterior, subarachnoidal, in the cerebellum subarachnoidal. The copy is poor, I can't read it here. Contusion, 0.5 times 0.5, around it, a small -- small dots of haemorrhage, 0.1. Lungs, left basal, plurae is -- is pasted, the heart and the aorta and the -- the heart, the aorta, and the pulmonal croagalins [as interpreted] are mixed. Liver, right subcapsular, 1 times 1. Gall-bladder, around -- there is around two cubic centimetres of gall. Spleen, pancreas, white, which means without any changes, without any distinguishing marks. Kidneys, left, indipalonic [as interpreted], blood. Urine contains blood. Stomach, 200 cubic centimetres of liquid contents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell us please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, liquid and mushy contents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Were these notes also incorporated into your final section protocol for Mr. Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All of them are incorporated in the internal findings of the section protocol.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could we turn, please, to page 4 of this document. And, Doctor, the document before you appears to have anatomical diagrams of the human head, and I draw your attention to the upper right corner of this diagram, has a face with some handwriting and markings on it. Again are these your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is this with respect to again the autopsy of Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And what do these markings on this particular diagram indicate?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the injuries found during the autopsy in the head area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And did you use the same methodology, meaning, did you describe the dimensions and the type of injury on this diagram as notes taken during the autopsy?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And were these also incorporated in your final written autopsy protocol?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the part that deals with the external description.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to please tender this entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P279, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness the section protocol for Atulla Qaili that we saw yesterday. It is again P00049, but could we please, for purposes of e-court pull up 65 ter 13.9. Again, this is tab 1 of the binders. If we could turn to page 2 of this document in both the English and the Macedonian version, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Dr. Jakovski, I'd like to take a look at some of the external injuries that you have noted on these sketches and then that were eventually incorporated into your section protocol with respect to Atulla Qaili. If we could go to the first full paragraph in the English and if I could direct your attention to paragraph 6, I believe, of the Macedonian version, which is paragraph 2 -- I mean, I'm sorry, page 2, paragraph 6 of the Macedonian version. There is a sentence that begins with: "The forehead is of medium height and slightly ridged." After that it says, "In the area of the right forehead region, there is a contusion of dark red violet colour. The epidermis is missing on its surface." And then it goes on to describe some other indications, and in the paragraph after that it begin with, "The eyes are with closed eyelids. The upper and lower lid of the left eye are entirely with a dark violet colour haematoma, while on the upper and lower lid of the right eye there is a dark violet colour haematoma." And then further down on this same page, and I believe it's actually on page 3, first full paragraph in the Macedonian version but further down on page 2 of the English version, it indicates that, the paragraph beginning with, "the nose has a regular configuration," it indicates that in the area of the upper third part of the ridge of the nose there is a contusion of dark red violet colour with the epidermis missing on its surface, oval-shaped," and gives dimensions. Then later on after that in the subsequent paragraph it goes on to say in the second sentence: "While dark red blood is flowing from the left external ear canal, in the area of the right earlobe there is a dark violet haematoma." Gives dimensions. And then following that it says, "In the area of the right cheek region there is a contusion of dark red violet colour with the epidermis missing from its surface." Dr. Jakovski, are those some of the injuries that you have noted in the diagrams that we have gone over already?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those are the injuries that are marked on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could then draw your attention, could we please display, tab 4 of the binders. It is already admitted as an Exhibit P00187. Dr. Jakovski, do you recognise the person depicted in this photograph that is displayed before you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that is the deceased Qaili Atulla.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this appears to be a close-up shot of his head, neck and upper chest region? At the time that you received the body for autopsy, did it look exactly like this?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The body was fresh. While in this photograph, one can see that the decomposition processes have already started.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So can you tell from this photograph that the photo was actually taken after the autopsy of Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Does your institute normally take photographs of the bodies that you perform autopsies on as normal protocol?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During any autopsy at our institute we take photographs and, if needed, also videorecording is made with the audiorecording accompanying it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And were photos actually taken as part of the protocol with respect to Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically, with regards to this case and the cases during the period of around five to six months, until before the start of the exhumation, we did not take photographs of the autopsies performed, because the photo camera was stolen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And I can ask you, notwithstanding the decomposition processes that you've noted in this particular photograph, in this photograph are the -- basically the contusion that you spoke of to the forehead area and the other injuries that we have just gone over with respect to the face, are these visible in this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are visible.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could look at the second photograph under tab 4, and if we could please display P00014. Again, doctor, do you recognise what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this appears to be a shot of the entire face of Atulla Qaili. Again, I'll ask you: At the time of autopsy, did his face look exactly like the photo here?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not look the same, because now there are changes to the colour of the skin, because of the initial decomposition, putrefaction processes, but the injuries are visible although they are disguised a bit during the -- partially disguised because of the decomposition processes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if question could take a look at this particular photograph, by the injuries being visible, do you mean this dark area that's right above what would be Atulla Qaili's left eye as well as on the left cheek?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see that the skin in the area around the injuries is red already in the area of the chin --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Or the beard, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- beard, moustache, as well as in the area of eyelids. It is already olive-green, which is a proof that the decomposition process has started.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And drawing your attention to the injuries right around the left eye area, specifically looking at these injuries, could you tell us, in your opinion what could have caused this type of injury?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The injuries in the head area have occurred as a result of use of dynamic blunt force.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please go back to the protocol which is at tab 1. Again, it's 65 ter 13.9. I'd like to draw your attention to page 3 of that document in the English version. And it is page 4, I believe, of the Macedonian version. And on this particular page, it's the third full paragraph of the Macedonian version and it is the third full paragraph of the English version. I'll draw your attention to the second sentence in that paragraph. It says: "In the area of the anterior lateral side of the right upper arm region there are four dark violet coloured haematomas that are strip-shaped and diagonally, longitudinally positioned with a direction from up and left towards down and right, they are parallel and from 13 to 6 centimetres in length and 1.5 centimetres in width." And later on in this same paragraph, there's a sentence that begins with, "In the area of the lateral side of the right shoulder, there is a dark violet coloured haematoma strip-shaped with dimensions 4.3 by 1.5 centimetres." Do you see that, Dr. Jakovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see 0.5 times 0.5.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall these injuries that I just read out to you? Do you recall also noting those in the diagram and in the final section protocol?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could then, please, if we could show the witness 65 ter 205. It's page 13 in e-court. Dr. Jakovski, I'll ask you again if you recognise what is depicted in this photo. It's actually photograph within tab 4 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this again appears to be the right arm and part of the chest area of Atulla Qaili; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And again, except for the changing in colour and some decomposition that you have already testified to as having occurred in prior photographs, is this a representation of what some of the injuries to the right arm were to the body at the time you saw it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention to the upper right arm area that is depicted in the photograph. There seem to be some lines or markings on the arm that are in a line formation or as, I think you termed it, strip-shaped. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Are those the particular injuries that we've just described in your protocol?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If you could, please, could you just circle with the - maybe the assistance of the usher - the particular injuries that you described as strip-shaped in your protocol.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could you please tell us, in your opinion, what could have caused this type of injury?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These type of injuries occur as a result of an instrument that was long, hard and blunt.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P280, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could stay in this tab of the binder, and if we could display 65 ter 205, page 5, it is another photograph within that tab 4. It bears ERN number N001-8133.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, again, Doctor, do you recognise the body of Atulla Qaili in this photograph as well?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this photograph appears to be a photo of the upper half of his body which includes his head. Again, notwithstanding the discolouration and decomposition changes that you have noted already with respect to the other photographs, are the injuries to the right arm and face visible in this photograph, that is, the injuries that you noted at the time of the autopsy?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are visible, but they're not as clear as they were during the autopsy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could draw your attention to the right -- what would the right arm of Atulla Qaili, and there seems to be again the strip-shaped marks and there seems to be one that is going -- actually follows from the right arm upwards to the chest area. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Was that an injury that you also noted in your autopsy protocol?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And the dark markings that are on the right hand and forearm of Atulla Qaili, were those also noted in your protocol and observed by you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could, with the usher's assistance, Dr. Jakovski, so we have a clear reception, could you please circle for us the injuries that you noted in your protocol and that are observable in this particular photograph.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could you also mark the ones that are still visible on the face.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And with respect to the left arm of Atulla Qaili are there any visible injuries that you noted in your protocol that are visible on this photograph as well?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should look at the sketch first. Could you help me and tell me in which tab are the sketches? I found them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, Doctor, I would like to ask you: Could you tell us in your opinion what could have caused these particular injuries?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These injuries have occurred as a result of a use of a dynamic, blunt, hard force.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could, please, stay in tab 4 of the binder and then we could display -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please tender this particular photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P281, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Staying in tab 4 of the binders, could we please display 65 ter 205? It's at page 7. It bears ERN N001-8135.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Doctor, do you recognise what is depicted in this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And there appears to be a photograph of the legs of Atulla Qaili. And again, except for the discolouration and changes you have noted with respect to decomposition, are injuries still visible that were visible to you at the time of autopsy in this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, please, Dr. Jakovski, could you please mark on this particular photograph the injuries that you noted at the time of autopsy?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And these particular injuries that have you noted on the legs, in your opinion, what could have caused these injuries?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These injuries have also occurred as a result of the activity of a dynamic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, application of a dynamic hard blunt force.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And were these particular injuries also set forth in your autopsy protocol in the section regarding external findings?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P282, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could we please go back to the section protocol. Again, it's tab 1 of the binders. It's 65 ter 13.9 for purposes of e-court. If we could please pull up page 5 of the English version of that particular document. I believe it is page 7 of the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Doctor, I would like to now discuss a little bit of the internal findings with respect this particular autopsy protocol. So I direct your attention to, I believe it is paragraph 6 of the English version and paragraph 6 on page 7 of the Macedonian version. There's a paragraph that starts: "The brain is slightly enlarged and of softer consistency. The lepto-meninges are smooth, glossy and under then in the area of the external side of the left front and top lobe there is a dark red bleeding distributed as a thin film." And then later on in the same paragraph it says: "In the area of the right frontal lobe in the basal part there a bleeding in the grey matter in the area of 0.5 by 0.5 centimetres." And then later on, second to last sentence of that paragraph it says: "Under the lepto-meninges" - I'll spell it for the record, l-e-p-t-o-m-e-n-i-n-g-e-s - "of the left hemisphere of the cerebellum there is a dark red bleeding distributed in the form of a film." And in the next paragraph, first sentence in the middle it starts: "Whereby in the area of the front left fosa cerebrea" - and this is page 8, first full paragraph of the Macedonian - "there is a linear crack that passes through the rear third of the fossa and then it continues up front," and it continues to describe that particular injury. Again, Doctor, are these particular areas some of the -- those that you noted with respect to the brain?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the injuries that have been written on the back side of the sketches which I read previously.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And did you also observe any external injuries to the head area besides the ones to the face and forehead that we have already discussed this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the injuries that have been described in the head area on the sketches are also part of the section protocol.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in the -- in your opinion, what could have caused these particular injuries, that is, the bleeding that's been noted and then this particular linear crack that you have described in your section protocol?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These injuries have occurred as a result of an application of a dynamic, blunt hard force in the area on the head.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please turn then to page 6 of the English, page 9 of the Macedonian, drawing your attention on the English version to paragraph 6, the first full paragraph 6, and paragraph 9 of the Macedonian on page 9. It indicates in reference to the paragraph that begins with "the kidneys have a normal size," the fourth or fifth sentence says: "The cortex is clearly divided from the pulp, while the tissue is of brownish-yellowish colour. In the calixes of the left kidney there is a liquid dark red-coloured blood while the calixes of the right kidney are empty. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And what is the significance of brownish-yellowish colour of the kidney?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The normal colour of the kidneys is brownish violet. In cases when there is some trauma or shock, the kidneys change their colour, and they become brownish and yellowish in colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And was there any external injury that you noted which might indicate what caused this particular injury to the kidney?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In projection of the left kidney, on the external or posterior side, at the level of the rib arch, there is a haematoma with a dimension 8 by 4 which is also described in the external description of the section protocol.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in your opinion, could this type of injury to the kidney be caused by a simple slap of the hand by somebody?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be very specific, but I wouldn't exclude the possibility with a very strong blow or hit by hand, by a box, by a fist that this type of injury might occur.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could draw your attention to the same page -- actually, I think it -- yes, same page in the Macedonian version, page 9. It's paragraph 10 of the Macedonian and it is the -- paragraph 11 or the second from last paragraph on page 6 of the English. That paragraph starts with: "After the removal of all internal organs," then it goes on in the next sentence to say: "On the left side of the chest broken ribs are noted in several lines, from the 2nd to the 9th ribs are broken from the parasternal line to the medial clavicular line, from the 2nd to the 10th rib are broken from medial clavicular line from to the medial axillary line, while the 7th rib is broken also in the clavicular line." In the last sentence it says, "Around the previously described broken places there is a dark red haematoma of the intercostal muscles." Do you see that, doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Okay. And am I reading this correctly to believe, then based on this, that there at least eight broken ribs found on Mr. Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And based on your experience, can you tell us what could have caused this particular type of injury?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Application or -- of a blunt force in the area of the chest.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could this type of injury have been caused by reanimation or what I would call resuscitation efforts?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When doing reanimation, broken ribs can occur. However, these where not located in the projections that have been concluded, found at the deceased body of Atulla Qaili.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could draw your attention next to page 7, the following page of the section protocol. I believe it is page 10 of the Macedonian version. There is a section in bold termed "Pathological Anatomical Diagnosis." Do you see that, doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And what follows is a list or a list of -- sorry, bullet points that go all the way to the following page. Can you tell us, please, what does this particular section describe or set forth?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the pathological anatomical diagnosis, describes all the injuries. In some other section protocols this part would include illnesses that have been concluded or found during the autopsy in Latin.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So this section, if you will, basically sets forth all of the injuries that are described in the section protocol?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could turn the page, please, in the English version to page 8. I believe it is page 12 -- 13 of the Macedonian version. There's a section towards the bottom that in bold says "opinion," and if I could read that, it says: "The death of the now deceased Atulla Qaili is violent and it occurred as a result of a traumatic shock." Next paragraph goes on to say: "The traumatic shock occurred as a result of a repeated action of a dynamic blunt and hard force in the area of the head, body, and limbs of the now deceased Atulla Qaili. And the following injuries point to this: haematomas, excoriations and contusions on the head, body and limbs, haematomas of the soft tissues of the head, haematoma in the subdural region, subarachnoidal bleeding, bleeding in the frontal parietal lobe of the brain, linear fraction in the area of the right and left frontal cranial pit, rib fractures on left chest in several lines, bleeding under the liver capsule and bleeding in the left kidney." And then it goes on to say: "As a result of the traumatic shock, a disturbance of the functioning and complete seizure of the functioning of important vital organs occurred, whereby a lethal outcome has happened to the now deceased Atulla Qaili." Do you see that, doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And bearing that in mind, if I could draw your attention and if we could please display to the doctor a document that is at tab 5 of the binder. It is 65 ter 220.1, bearing ERN N000-5180 - N000-5180 [sic]. Doctor, the document that is before you, if I could just draw your attention to the top. It says "medical report." It goes on to say, "Abdula Cajani, from the village of Ljuboten," and it says under that "admitted 13 August 2001." And then it says "Exitus letl 13 August 2001" and in that paragraph it says: "On 13 August 2001, Abdula Cajani was admitted to the clinic with injuries to the head, neck and body, heteroanamnestic - I apologise - data for an injury resulting from a fall." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this document was shown to me in Skopje when we have been -- I have been interviewed, but I don't recall precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At the time of performing the autopsy on Atulla Qaili, did you see this document, had you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Drawing your attention to the indication that it was an injury resulting from a fall, is that consistent with your findings based on your autopsy of Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These injuries are not consistent with falling down.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could you please tell us in your opinion what these injuries were consistent with?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With direct application of a dynamic, blunt, hard force.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is it based on a combination of all of the injuries that caused Atulla Qaili's death?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the autopsy of the deceased, Atulla Qaili, we have concluded injuries in the head area, such as bleeding under the -- aponeurose helmet and the brain membrane and broken bones in the base of the skull which, on their own can be considered as a serious bodily injury, injury that endangers the life of the patient. But also, other broken ribs have been found on the left-hand side of the chest which have made breathing rather difficult, and of course -- of course pain, and all these injuries have caused a very difficult shock situation, which is also corroborated by the change in the kidneys, which is the reason or the cause of death.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we tender this document that is displayed before us, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P283, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could next draw your attention and if we could display for the witness 65 ter 1002, which is located at 6 of today's binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Doctor, drawing your attention to the upper left corner of this particular document it says general city hospital, surgery, Skopje, and then it indicates ward, traumatology, and there's a date, 13 August 2001. And then right below that in handwriting it says -- there's a plus and it says exodus at 1330 hours and in the middle it says history of illness and then the first name to the left, it says Abdulla and the last name below that says Cajani. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you again recognise this particular name, Abdula Cajani?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the name of the person when he was admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And later on this is the person who was later determined to be Atulla Qaili; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And drawing your attention to the bottom of the document, if we could scroll down on both versions, please. There's a signature at the very bottom, it says chief of ward and it indicates assistant, Dr. S. Vuckov. Do you see?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And have you seen these types of documents before from the general city hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes along with the body we would receive these types of documents, and for the specific case we did not have a discharge list, that is to say, the history of the illness. However, it doesn't always happen in practice, although we insist, as an institute, to have the whole history of the illness of any deceased patients. The hospitals generally send to us only the mortuary notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is this document what would look like to be a typical medical file for a patient from Skopje city hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the file that -- for a patient that was admitted in the city hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention, please, and if we could display page 2 of both documents, both versions. And at the very top of this document in bold it indicates "case history," and then skipping down it says, "current illnesses," and then it indicates that "patient admitted as urgent case due to head and neck injuries and contusions on the body as a result of a fall." Do you see that, doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And again that is the result of a fall, that is not consistent with your findings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we please tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P284, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Dr. Jakovski, as part of the autopsy for Atulla Qaili, did you also take blood samples for the purposes of toxicology and blood alcohol screenings?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the autopsy, from the body of the deceased we have taken blood and urine samples in order to prove possible presence of ethyl alcohol, drugs or medicaments.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt my colleague. Simply, about the document that has just been tendered, we would like to know whether the entire document has been admitted or only the first two pages, because we would wish to use perhaps the same parts but also other parts of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe the whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And drawing your attention to tab 7, which is 65 ter 996, if we could please display that. Dr. Jakovski, looking at this document, in the upper left corner it says, forensic and criminological institute, Skopje, and then on the right side it says assistant DZ Jakovski and then it goes on to say that on 14/8/2001, Dr. Jakovski performed an autopsy over the deceased person and then it indicates that there was a toxicology analysis, biological material was taken off to determine presence of psychotropic substances, medicines, and ethyl alcohol. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then afterwards it says in bold laboratory finding and then it goes on to indicate negative results for these particular substances that are listed. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then it also indicates later on that it says ethyl alcohol K, ethyl alcohol U, and indicates zero per cent. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Were these the particular findings with respect to Atulla Qaili's biological samples and blood?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P285, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Dr. Jakovski, are you familiar with the paraffin glove test?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Was a paraffin glove test formed on Atulla Qaili's hands at some point.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, before the giving of the autopsy, we conducted the paraffin glove test used to prove probable presence of nitrates and nitrites.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And can I ask you with respect to -- well, can we please show the doctor P00049, page 33, English, and page 110 Macedonian. It is tab 9 of today's binders. Doctor, the document in front of you indicates at the very top left corner, if we could perhaps minimise the -- yes, thank you. "University Kiril i Metodij," and then it goes on to say, working unit forensic institute and criminology related to SP 11918-245. Indicates a date of 15 August 2001, Skopje. And then in the next sentence it says -- relates to a number and a date and it says about now deceased Qaili Atulla, paraffin gloves were taken off his left and right hand during the autopsy." And right underneath the words "laboratory analysis" it indicates that there was one nitrate-nitrite particle on its back side on the lower phalange of the index finger, two nitrate-nitrite particles at the root of the thumb, and five nitrate-nitrite particles on a height of the wrist. And then it goes on to describe other findings. Now, at the very bottom it says analysis were read by, it indicates a Professor Dr. Aleksa Duma and then it indicates assistant Dr. Zlatko Jakovski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: As a doctor in forensic medicine, you indicated that you deal with the paraffin glove test through your Forensic Institute. Do you also keep abreast of the literature and studies relating to this particular test as well as other types of tests relating to the presence of nitrates?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Around the world there are much more sophisticated methods than this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And with respect to this particular test, this paraffin glove test, if nitrate particles are detected, is this conclusive evidence that someone actually fired a weapon?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether the Your Honours will be -- will allow for me to briefly describe the logic behind the paraffin glove test.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all I would like to say that proving through -- powder particles through the diphenylamine method which is being used when conducting the paraffin glove test is a non-specific method. Because in this way you can prove only the presence of nitrates and nitrites, which besides in gunpowder particles can be found also in fertilisers, photographic material, people working in the pharmaceutical industry, people who smoke cigarettes. However, with the paraffin glove test, one can prove the precise location of the nitrates and nitrates, and if one performs a trial shot with the precise weapon, in such case, this can be used as evidence. That is why we use this method at our institute, unfortunately, just this one method, because of our limit the financial possibilities at our institute for purchasing of equipment required for more sophisticated modern methods and technologies in order to prove the presence of powder particles.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I guess my question to you, doctor, was with respect to this test, then, is it a conclusion that one can draw, an absolute conclusion, that if particles are found that this -- the particular person that was tested actually fired a weapon or even held a weapon?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With this particular method, one can only prove the presence of nitrates and nitrites, and specifically to prove whether this person shot a gun, one has to perform a trial shot using the very same weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can I ask you, doctor, were the hands of Atulla Qaili protected or preserved in some way when the body came for autopsy?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hands of the deceased were not protected.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you mentioned in your prior answer that particles can be found in other common products, everyday products. Can I ask you, could the lack of preservation of the hands lead to contamination as well?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One cannot exclude the possibility for the hands to be contaminated.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Are paraffin glove tests requested in every autopsy performed in your institute?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Paraffin glove tests are done in cases the deceased ones have participated in some shooting or where there are suspicions concerning a given case of shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And who decided to do the particular paraffin test in the case of Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Professor Duma and myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So no outside body requested that you perform the test?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, that last document, I believe has already been admitted. So I with like to move on to tab 10 of today's binder. It is 65 ter 279.3. It bears ERN N001-7427.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Dr. Jakovski, I'd just like to show you a couple of additional documents. Does the document, the second -- well, let start at the top here. The upper left-hand corner it says clinic for surgical diseases and then it lists the place Skopje, and in the middle it says discharge paper. Indicates right below that the insured person Cajani Abdula. It says village, Ljuboten. And then goes on to say admitted to hospital treatment on 13 August 2001 and discharged on 13 August 2001. And then below it lists with the diagnosis, I believe there are some Latin medical terms there. And it says operation, stitching of wounds. And then it says directions for further treatment. And the second sentence of that paragraph says: "The history of decease received from others than the patient gave an information that the injury was caused by falling down." And in the very last sentence it says: "At around 1330 hour, a sudden death of the patient occurred." At the time of the autopsy -- I know that you have testified to receiving some type of discharge paper typically when you receive autopsies. At the time of Atulla Qaili's autopsy, had you received this particular discharge paper?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could draw your attention, yesterday you indicated that typically in additional paperwork that you get with the body, you usually get a description of the diagnosis and injury. If I could draw your attention to the last paragraph that I read where it says directions for further treatment, does that information contained in that paragraph reflect what typically would be given to you as part of the autopsy paperwork?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we are given sometimes such documents, then the epicrisis of mortuary note -- then the mortuary note of the epicrisis states these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And could I ask you if you had this particular information, for example, the sentence I read to you about the injury was caused by falling down, if you had had this particular information, would that have changed your opinion regarding the cause of death?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the epicrisis, the doctor gives the data that he receives when he -- when the patient is brought as he is told in the original way, and it is his duty to write them down in that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the concrete case, we can write down these remarks, that they exist, as such, but as forensics, we know which injury, how it occurred, from what it was caused; therefore, even if we had this information, we would have given the same opinion as we have given it in the section protocol.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P286, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 11 of today's binders, which is 65 ter 279.7. It bears ERN N001-7431.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, doctor, drawing your attention to the upper part of this document, in the middle says certificate. It goes on to say the city general hospital, and then goes on to say Abdula Cajani from the village Ljuboten, who died on 13 August 2001 at 1339 hours. And it lists a diagnosis and then it has a seal there. Do you recognise this seal as one that would typically come from the city general hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the seal of the city hospital of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And did you have this particular document at the time of the autopsy of Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P287, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could next turn to tab 12 of today's binder, if we could display for the witness 65 ter 279.5.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Doctor, drawing your attention to the left portion of this document in the middle there it says death certificate and then it lists first and last name, maiden name at number 1, and I believe the words we can make out is at least first name of Atulla, lists at number three date of death 13 August 2001, and at number 4 place of death, city hospital Skopje, and then if we could scan over to the right side of the document, both versions, towards the bottom it says signature, I believe there is a seal there. Signature of pathologist and it says Dr. Zlatko Jakovski. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then if we could, please, scan back over to number, I believe -- well, it's 11-B on the right side. And it indicates there that the death was and there is an underscore or a box checked as violent. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And did you actually issue this particular death certificate yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a certificate issued by our institute.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is this -- just for the record, is this pertaining to the same Atulla Qaili that you've already testified about?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P288, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Then if we could turn to tab 13 of today's binder, and if we could show for the witness 65 ter 999.1, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Doctor, drawing your attention to the upper left corner, this document says WU forensic and criminological institute, gives a number and then it gives a date of 22/5/2003, says Skopje underneath. It says to Basic Court Skopje II and has a Judge Dragan Niklovski and then indicates as the subject, delivery of autopsy protocols for exhumations in Ljuboten village. And then in the first paragraph it says that these exhumations were performed upon your order in the time from 9 April 2003 to 23 April 2003, in presence of observers from the ICTY. And then the last paragraph, I believe on both pages it says: "In this context we would like to mention that this is our first serious and official conversation regarding the critical incident with both representatives of the Macedonian judiciary and the international community." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 of the document in both versions. At the very bottom of this page it says in the name of the professional staff, professor Dr. Aleksa Duma, and then to the left it says delivered to and it lists these persons, prime minister of the government of RM Ministry of Interior of RM, minister of justice of RM, ambassador of US in RM. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the exhumations that took place in Ljuboten village that are referred to in this particular correspond?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recognise this signature of Dr. Aleksa Duma?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And are you aware of the contents of this particular letter? That is to say, were you informed that this particular correspondence was written by Dr. Duma at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This correspondence was done by a smaller number of professors at the institute. But, in general, at the professional meetings that we have, at the staff meetings that we have, the wider staff was informed about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P289, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Dr. Jakovski, did anyone from the Macedonian police ever contact you regarding the circumstances of Atulla Qaili's death?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few days after the autopsy. I don't remember how many days after the autopsy --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm sorry, doctor. My question was -- well, let me ask you this. You said you don't remember how many days after the autopsy. Could you tell us who you were contacted by?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was contacted by inspectors from the identification department with a court order to conduct an exact identification of the person -- of the person Atulla Qaili because in our institute he was admitted under another name, Abdula Cajani.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And was that the substance of your conversation with this particular inspector?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And other than that, did you have any conversations with anyone from the Macedonian police regarding your autopsy findings with respect to Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- no. I didn't have any conversation, me personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will now have the first break and will resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, doctor. My name is Guenael Mettraux and together with my colleague Edina Residovic, I'm appearing on behalf of Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps before we start, we'll have binders of document distributed to the Court, to the witness, and we also have a copy for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, before we start with the substance of your evidence, I would like to ask you a few questions about the structure and position of your substitute. Is it correct that the institute, the Forensic Institute is independent from the government?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Forensic Institute and Criminology is part of the medical faculty in Skopje within the university Kiril and Metodij. The autonomy of the institute is guaranteed with the very autonomy of the university. And in that respect we are an independent research and scientific institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Doctor, that the only link, if I may use that term, with the state authorities is with the ministry of education because your institute also provides education to medical students. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only link to the government of the Republic of Macedonia is related to the part which is funded by the ministry of education concerning the -- the lectures that we provide to the medical school students to the stomatology [as interpreted] and to the law faculty. All are the services that are offered by the institute whose final beneficiaries are the courts of the Republic of Macedonia, the interior ministry, and the legal entities of the Republic of Macedonia. In that respect, we work for them on -- upon the grounds of free economic cooperation, which means that all of them, for our services, pay in accordance with the price list of the services provided by the institute. .

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, sir, if an organ or an institution of the states requires your services, do I understand properly that they would have to pay for those services. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For each service of ours there is a price and they have to pay it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that the government or its ministries cannot give you any orders or instructions as pertains to your work. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one can give any order related to the way we should work. We only get orders from investigating judges to conduct an autopsy or some other forensic expertise, but this is not an order which says how and in which way to do it, but it is only an order to collect evidence for a given case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps to pick on your last answer, you indicated that yesterday that such a request for an autopsy could only come - and correct me if I'm wrong - from the investigative judge according to the criminal procedure or from the hospital in relation to the law on health. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the request -- or the police does not have the authority or the power under the law of Macedonia to make such a request to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police does not have the right to issue an order for autopsy pursuant to the laws of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply to wrap up with the information about your institute, sir, is that correct that today as well as in 2001 the director of the institute was Professor Duma?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Professor Dr. Aleksa Duma is still the director of the Forensic Institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I would like you to assist if you may with a few general questions about the way in which deceased person are brought to your institute, and I will take you a few steps back. Could the witness please be shown document which is under tab 7 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Exhibit P259. Under the ERN N000-5166 - N00-5166-ET and the Macedonian version of that document is N005-0574 - N005-0574.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have that document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we way focus first on the top left-hand corner of the document, you can see that it comes from the sector of interior, Skopje, department of interior, Cair, and more specifically, the Mirkovic -- Mirkovci police station. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is submitted by Dragan Surlov on the 13th of August, 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it's an Official Note number 1192; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the subject of that Official Note is as follows: "Qaili Atulla, medical assistance requested for detained person taken to GOB, city hospital." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there is a text that follows. It says this: "On 13 August 2001 at 1430" --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we have corrected this mistake. The original says 4.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "Atulla Qaili asked for medical assistance. I called an ambulance which arrived in the police station and they said that the person must be taken to a hospital. I informed the sector of the interior, Major Ilija Dzambaski as well as deputy operations centre of Skopje, who allowed the person to be taken to the city hospital," and it's signed by Dragan Surlov. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, that the ambulance service in Macedonia is under the overall system an organisation of the hospital services in the country?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the ambulance service functions as a separate unit with -- in the relation to the hospitals.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it falls institutionally within the responsibility of the hospital system; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, once a patient is brought to the hospital, is that correct that he or she would be registered upon arrival?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the responsibility to register him in the hospital registries would be with the doctor on duty. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The team on duty, the doctor, the nurse and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is now P283. Doctor, it is under tab number 8 in your binder. You will recall that my colleague has shown you the document a bit earlier. And if I can focus --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... your attention on the third line in that document it says that Mr. Abdula Cajani was admitted on 13 August 2001 by Dr. Nabasa Nastov, intern. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would that be the person who, in fact, entered the datas and information upon the arrival and registration of Mr. Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably yes, since he signed the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that upon registration, the doctor on duty or the person who does the registration form would record a number of information about the patient that has been brought to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The doctor enters all the information he gets from the patient or from the persons that have brought him. He enters the information just the way they have been told to him. He must not add anything or change anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would that include the name of the patient, if it is known to the doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the name as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, doctor, that the doctor on duty doesn't know at that time the name of the patient, he would generally enter an X in place of the name of the person?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually it's an MM, an unknown -- which means an unknown person.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could the witness please be shown what is now P284. It will be the 8th page of that document in the English. And--

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, doctor, it is tab 9 of your binder. And it's again part of this history or medical record of Mr. Qaili, and under the name and surname, can you see an inscription saying "X, male"? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that if the name of the person, of the patient becomes known to the doctor on duty later during that day, the name would then be recorded as understood and learned by him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can please move to what is page 4 of the same document, still P284. Do you have that document, sir? It says: "Admittance record for patient." We're trying to find the Macedonian version, doctor, for you. I think I have it. I think it is page 9. It would be ERN N006-3761. It's page 9 of the Macedonian. Do you have the document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as you can see under this document it says "Admittance record for patient." It is still dated the 13th of August 2001. And under the name and last name of the patient it is written "Cajani Abdula." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go to point 6 of that document it says: "Admitted to hospital on 13 August 2001, 5.00 on trauma ward as emergency." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, sir, perhaps are you able to recognise the signature that is on the Macedonian version of that document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the signature, but I can -- I don't know whose signature this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to read a passage of a statement taken from Dr. Nastov by the Prosecution. It is Rule 65 ter 1D231, 1D002497.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honour, we don't have a Macedonian version of that document. If I could ask the registry to move to the third page of that document at paragraph 8, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, I'll read the paragraph to you since there is no Macedonian version. It says this: "I can't remember anymore the precise time when I received the first person from Ljuboten. But I can refer to the date and time, looking into the records of this person. According to the file, it was 5.00 in the morning of the 13 August 2001. I can confirm the entries in the medical file. I identify my handwriting and my signatures." Sir, would that be consistent with the document I've just shown you and the information which was contained in that document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now, looking at paragraph 9 further down - again I'll read it out to you. It says this: "I can't remember who delivered the patient. But I can say that I was admitting the patient as 'X man.' That means he was admitted as an unidentified male person." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I was not aware that the patient was somehow related to the events in Ljuboten until I finished my shift. I can't remember if this person was guarded by the police or not." Then goes on to say, there a sentence -- two sentences, and it says: "Reading the file I used the term not approachable, which means he was conscious but disorientated. I didn't want to communicate or the language barrier prevented a communication. I can't remember if I had a conversation with him. Being asked from whom I received the information written in the medical file that the person was falling down, I say this information came probably from the patient himself. He probably told me this." Then goes on to say this: "I have been shown the dismissal letter signed by me on 13 August 2001 in which I used the term heteroanamnesticki. I agree this term would indicate that I learned about the patient's history from somebody else other than the patient. Today, I can only explain that this might have been a small slip on my side. I say that the patient's history written on the second page of the medical file is more accurate and was written at the time when I admitted the patient. In this version, the above-mentioned term is not mentioned. I therefore think that the patient told me by himself that he was fallen down." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would that account be consistent with the documents that I've shown you and which have been shown to you by my colleague of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It corresponds to the data that were shown by the Prosecutor's office and also it is written here that he had fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think we've understood from your evidence that the person who entered the name of the patient in the record would have been Dr. Nastov himself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the last thing that you have shown me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I may ask you to go to the next page of that statement, sir. This would be the next page for the registry, paragraph 13, 1-3. This is what Dr. Nastov told the Prosecution, Doctor: "Being asked, I say probably the nurses told me in the afternoon of 13 August 2001 the name Abdula Cajani as the person's name I received as unknown X man. I, by myself, don't know where this name came from." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Consistent with the two documents I have just shown you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then, Dr. Nastov is asked by the Prosecution in paragraph 15, if we can move down a bit, and he's answered this: "Being asked about the identity of the person that I admitted as X man, I have to say that I have learned only a few days ago that the person had obviously two different identities." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you a few questions about the transfer of a deceased person from the city hospital to your institute. Is that correct that such transport is the responsibility, once again, of the ambulance and also the hospital system?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bodies are transported from a hospital or from another location to our institute by the cemetery company - its name is Butel - and not by an ambulance.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that the morgue in Butel is part of the municipal system? It's not part of any of the ministries. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a joint stock company. It has been privatized.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But at the time in 2001, is that correct that it was part of the municipality of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You have been asked by my colleague about document which you received about -- together with the body of Mr. Qaili. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've said that at the time you received only one page, and you indicated that there was nothing unusual in that respect; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also that there is was no reason for you to query this matter further to ask the hospital, on the second page, if any had gone missing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't have the right to investigate. That is part of the tasks of the investigative bodies, primarily the investigating judge. We are a service for the court. We are not a law enforcement body.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct also, doctor, that the responsibility to transmit the paperwork or the papers from the hospital was with the administrative department of the city hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is their competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a few question about the autopsy of Mr. Qaili which you've carried out. And if you could turn to page -- to tab 13 of your binder, sir. This is again the section protocol which was shown to you by my colleague a bit earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, just as a matter of clarification, we'll use P49, which is ET N0010095-01. The reason for this, Your Honour, is at this stage this is the translation which is part of this document which is slightly different than the translation used by my colleague, and since it hasn't been formally exchanged we will use this one. The content is similar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, it is also in your binder at tab 1-3, if it is more practical for you to look at the paper version. You have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I may quickly go through the first part of that document. It refers to the autopsy having been performed on 14 August 2001, and as you have indicated, it suggests that it's been done on request of the general city hospital Naum Ohridski Skopje. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a section which is entitled data on the subject of the case, and it says this: "From the mortuary certificate which was issued by the general city hospital, Sv. Naum Ohridski, this data was obtained and bearing the name of the deceased Qaili Atulla was entered as Abdula Cajani with the following diagnosis." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then it goes on to cite the diagnosis in question. Then the next sentence says this: "On 16 August 2001, a written report was delivered by the investigative judge of the Basic Court Skopje II, Skopje, where it is cited that the name of the person Qaili Atulla in the mortuary certificate was entered as Abdula Cajani by mistake." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you've indicated already that there was nothing unusual about a request being made for an autopsy by the hospital itself, is that correct; it was in fact was quite frequent?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, sir, that any requests for an autopsy, whether it comes from the investigative judge or from the hospital, is being sent to the institute and more specifically to Professor Duma and not to the other doctors within that institute?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any request for an expert report, including the autopsies, are addressed to the institute and not to an individual doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would Professor Duma be the person responsible to deal with those requests?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Professor Duma reviews the requests and is involved -- informed about the overall daily operation of the institute. And mainly the autopsies are performed by the duty team and there is a monthly schedule for that team.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, can you recall that two days or so after the autopsy had been performed a request from the investigative judge for information and identification of Mr. Qaili was sent to the institute?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A request was sent by an investigating judge in order to ascertain the true identity of the person Atulla Qaili.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, sir, did Professor Duma at the time show you that document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably yes. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
