utterances.text: Can the witness now be shown what is Exhibit P54, with an ERN ET-N001-9697-009, and it is under tab 14 of your binder. The Macedonian version is N001-9643-055.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can go and look at the top left-hand corner of that document it says Lower Court Skopje II, Skopje, investigative judge, and then there is a number which is 436-01 and a date, 14 August 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Title of the document is Official Note. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention to the first paragraph of that document. It says this: "On 14 August 2001 I visited the city general hospital in Skopje and talked with Dr. Viktor Kamilovski with regard to the health condition of the following detained individuals." And then he goes on to list four names. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the fourth name is Mr. Atulla Qaili; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next paragraph it records the following information: "Individuals Bajrami Nevaip and Ramadani Ismail were admitted to the city general hospital on Skopje on 13 August 2001 at approximately 2115 hours with Ametovski Adem at 2320 and Qaili Atulla at 5 hours on 13 August 2001." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... So the timing of the registration or arrival of Mr. Qaili at the city hospital is correct. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can jump over the next paragraph to go over the paragraph which starts the word "Qaili Atulla," it says this: "Qaili Atulla was admitted on 8 August at 5 hours but succumbed to his injury on the same day at 1339 hours. However, he is registered in medical documentation under the name Abdula Cajani, born 3 November 1965 in Skopje, with residence in the village of Ljuboten, according to information provided during his admittance." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then an order was handed down for an autopsy to be performed on his body at the forensic institute at the medical faculty in Skopje. Can see this?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then in the next paragraph it goes on to recount another visit that the judge paid at the city hospital and it is signed by investigative Judge Velce Pancevski. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I have a few question about the procedure of the autopsy. Is that correct that generally when the investigative judge make a request for an autopsy, he would be present during the autopsy itself?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It very rarely happens that an investigating judge is present at an autopsy. Mainly they only issue an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as far as the police is concerned, is that correct that they can attend if invited by the judge to do so?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is also a very rare occurrence that the police is present at an autopsy, but if it is needed for them to collect some evidence during the autopsy, then we invite them and we then hand that evidence over to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And who would invite them? Would that be your institute or would that be the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that the police cannot supervise the process of autopsy even if they are present during the procedure?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could not supervise it or make any instructions or -- on what we should do and how we should do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply to correct a mistake which appears to be a mistake of mine at page 47, line 15, it says 8th of August, and I believe it should say 13th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is this correct, sir, that if the police attends an autopsy of a deceased, the presence of the police would be noted in the autopsy protocol?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually we do not record this. If they are present there, they're just present as technical personnel and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the police is present, would you make a specific annotation to that effect?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we do not do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think you've indicated that there was a bit of uncertainty at some stage about the exact identity of Mr. Qaili. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also that the investigative judge queried the matter with your institute?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. An investigating judge requested for an accurate identification of the person to be performed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could this witness please be shown Exhibit P54, which is ET N001-9712 and the Macedonian version is N001-9643-070. Your Honour, this is under tab 15 of the binder, 1-5.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have that document, doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Top left-hand corner, it says Basic Court Skopje II, Skopje. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Skopje II, Skopje, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And underneath that there is a line of question marks. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply at this stage we would like to point this. The original Macedonian of the document, as you can see from the copy, is also illegible as far as the date is concerned. However, in the exhibit tendered by the Prosecution, P55, there is the exact same letter, the very same letter, with an ERN of N001-9713. And in that version, the date is clearly legible as being the 16 of August 2001. We will make a request in due course to have that other letter translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Doctor, can we go on now to the right-hand corner. You can see it is sent to the Institute of Forensic Medicine at the medical faculty, Skopje. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps before I go further into the text, you recognise this letter as the one that had been shown you by Dr. Duma, Professor Duma at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if we go back -- if we go down a bit to the subject header it says, "Request on identification of a person Qaili Atulla." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we focus on the first paragraph it records the following: "With a decision made by the investigative judge at the Basic Court Skopje II, Skopje, under KY number 436-01, dated 14 August 2001, an investigation has been implemented against accused Qaili Atulla." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And further done in this same paragraph, the first paragraph, it says that detention has been imposed together with other accused in period of 30 days considering from 14 August 2001 at 12.30 to 13 September 2001 at 12.30 because of existence of legal basis from Article 184, paragraph 1, items 1, 2, and 3, from the ZKP because of the well-founded suspicion he has committed criminal act terrorism due to Article 313, from KZ," that is the criminal code. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the next paragraph mentions the following: "During the investigative procedure the investigative judge has been informed by the Ministry of Interior of Republic of Macedonia, SVR Skopje, OVR Cair, Skopje, that accused Atulla Qaili because his health condition got worse has been transferred with an ambulance vehicle to the general city hospital, Skopje for medical treatment on 13 August 2001 at about 4.30 but during the day he has died." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Documents we have seen earlier?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then it goes on to say this: "On 14 August 2001 the investigative judge has visit the general city hospital Skopje and he has had a conversation with Dr. Kamilovski and Dr. Nikola Gruev, who is director of the general city hospital Skopje. And therein he has been informed that accused Qaili Atulla has been brought and received at the general city hospital Skopje on 13 August 2001 at 5.00 and he died the same day, 13 August 2001, at 1339." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, that is consistent with the documents which we've discussed earlier?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then it goes to say: "The general city hospital Skopje has hand over the body of the deceased to the Institute for Forensic Medicine at the medical faculty Skopje for autopsy." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again that would be consistent with what you have seen and said before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next paragraph says a certificate of -- a certificate, a dismissal letter with a history of illness has been prepared with a number of 3020-2001 by the general city hospital Skopje and also a mortuary enclosure dated from 13 August 2001. But the medical documentation on person Abdula Cajani has been issued when this person has been registered under this name and last name when he has been received at general city hospital Skopje. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And finally it says: "Concerning the fact of differences in name and last name of the deceased person, whereas the possibility it is same person Qaili Atulla is a matter of fact, we need to be informed if it is the same person Atulla Qaili and if identification, autopsy, and medical testimony have been performed so that the investigative judge can proceed in accordance with a court of the criminal procedure." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is signed by Velce Pancevski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Is that consistent with your recollection of this document and the discussion you had with Professor Duma at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, there's another document I'd like to show you now. It is it Prosecution Rule 65 ter 381 with an ERN N000-1255-ET and the Macedonian version is N000-1255. And it is under tab 16 of your binder. Is that correct, sir, that the responsibility to establish the identity of a deceased person is with the investigative judge and not with your institute?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask you to focus on the top left-hand corner of that document, once again it says primary court Skopje II, Skopje, investigation department, and again the same number 436-01 with the date 16 August 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is it addressed to the prison Skopje, Skopje for the director. Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then a subject title and a reference title with again the number of the case and date, 14 August 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph it again referred to an investigation procedure by the same number against a number of individuals and if you look at the third line there's the name Qaili Atulla. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And further down in that it mentions the fact that detention measures have been ordered against those people by the investigative judge on 14 August 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there is a second paragraph starting with the word "in order to determine," which says the following: "In order to determine the identification of the detained person Qaili Atulla," and then there's a number of datas about this person, "the investigating judge referred with a letter KINO number 436-01 dated 16 August 2001 to the Institute for Forensic Medicine at the faculty of medicine, Skopje and to the ministry of internal affairs of Republic of Macedonia, directorate for internal affairs, Skopje, sector for administrative affair in order to collect data-identification of the detained person and an excerpt from the registered of the deceased." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As far as it refers to the faculty or the Institute for Forensic Medicine, this passage would be consistent with the letters that I have shown you just previously. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the follow is recorded: "From the submitted medical documentation from the general city hospital, Skopje, the investigative judge determined that the person listed under the name Abdula Cajani from the village Ljuboten, Skopje, who was accepted at the general city hospital, Skopje on 13 August 2001 at 5 hours is the same deceased person on 13 August 2001 at 1339." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again it is signed by the investigative judge Pancevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D67, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, you've indicated, I believe, that you were able to state the real name of Mr. Qaili in the section protocol in your evidence in chief. I think you mentioned that you met with relatives of Mr. Qaili. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that you were able to do so because of the letter of the investigative judge that you received on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that Mr. Pancevski visited your institute after had you performed the autopsy on to Mr. Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he visited. I cannot recall. I can't be certain, but I believe that he visited it personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- perhaps I can assist you there, doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is P54 with an ERN N001-N699-ET-001, and the Macedonian version of that document is under the ERN N001-9643-184.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, you can turn to tab 17, 1-7, of your binder. Do you have the document, doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you look at the top left-hand corner of this document it again says Basic Court Skopje II, Skopje, investigative unit, again the same number 436-01 and it's dated 20 August 2001 can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is again an Official Note and it is signed by investigative Judge Velce Pancevski. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you go on to the first paragraph it says this: "On 20 August 2001 at 8.45 hours I have been at the Institute for Forensic Medicine at the medical faculty Skopje regarding to the investigative case KIN 036-01. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it goes on to say: "And in relation with the letter delivered to the medical faculty, Skopje to collect data and identification on accused Qaili Atulla from the village of Ljuboten, Skopje." Then in the next paragraph it said: "I had a conversation with Professor Dr. Boskovski and Dr. Zlatko Jakovski and I have been informed of the following. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says from the general city hospital, Skopje, clinic for surgery, diseases, Skopje, on "14 August 2001 the deceased person has been brought to the institute for forensic medicine and medical documentation. Death certificate, letter of dismissal with illness history number 3020-01, and a letter to the mortuary subsidiary entered with name Cajani Abdula from the village of Ljuboten, Skopje. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It also says: "An autopsy and court medical testimony has been obtained and a section protocol SP number 11918-245-01 dated from 14 August 2001 has been prepared by Dr. Aleksa Duma and Dr. Zlatko Jakovski." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Refresh your memory about the events and the meeting with Judge Pancevski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a last paragraph, sir, which relates to papillary lines, and I will read it to you. It says this: Papillary lines have been drawn out of the deceased person and a procedure of identification is in the course." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct, sir, that this procedure was not carried out by you or by the institute. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This procedure for the identification by using the papillary lines is conducted by the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, will -- the document is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to ask you a number of matters about the nature of your responsibilities as far as your work is concerned. Is that correct that your responsibility and conclusions as far as an autopsy is concerned are purely medical and scientific in nature?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the conclusions that you draw are not of a legal character. That's for the investigative judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They don't have a legal character, but just a scientific one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the responsibility to find out, for instance, what happened with the body of Mr. Qaili would be with the investigative judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to read out to you a passage taken from a statement of a person called Jovan Serafimovski. We will try to find the ERN number so you can have it in front of you in due course. At this stage I would like to read this paragraph for you. It is taken from an OTP statement of Mr. Serafimovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document has been marked for identification as 1D227 and it has an ERN 1D002452. It was not marked for identification but it has that number. And if can I ask the registry to go to the first page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As you can see, sir, this is a statement by the Office of the Prosecutor of Mr. Jovan Serafimovski. He is current occupation is public prosecutor, basic public prosecutor's office Skopje, and his former occupation was deputy public prosecutor, basic public prosecutor's office Skopje, and it was taken on the 19th and 20th of 2005. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... And ask the registry to move on to the next page, paragraph 7. That would be the next page. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, this is what Mr. Serafimovski is recorded as saying to the Office of the Prosecutor: "In the request to conduct an investigation submitted on 14 August 2001, the name of Qaili Atulla is mentioned. It was my obligation to ascertain the cause of death. I asked the investigative judge, Velce Pancevski, to inquire about this. We found that Cajani Adbula was injured during a clash with the police and army in Ljuboten. I was informed from the media that the police and army were there." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "I don't know which units were there. We never received information like this. I did not ask for information like this. We did not ask because we were told that many people were involved." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say: "The only information that I had about the whereabouts of Qaili Atulla prior to dealt is that Mr. Atulla was in the hospital. Today, for the first time I learned that Mr. Atulla was detained in the police station at Mirkovci. I first found out about his injuries from the death certificate provided by the investigative judge." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your experience as a forensic expert, is what Mr. Serafimovski consistent with the obligations and duties of state prosecutors?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask the registry to move on to the next page and to focus on paragraph 10 of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Serafimovski says this: "With respect to the case of Qaili Atulla referred to under number 7, I was not aware on 14 August 2001 that the accused QA was already dead. I learned about the death of QA by receiving written information from the investigative Judge Velce Pancevski. It was my obligation to find out of the cause of the death of QA. We learned that he had was injured during a clash with the Macedonian security forces in Ljuboten." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you look at paragraph 11 of the statement he says: "I don't know about the circumstances of QA's depth. The only information I have about the whereabouts of QA before he died is that he was in the hospital. I don't know what QA did before he died or where he was before he died." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can go back up a little bit into paragraph 10 once again. Towards the end of this paragraph Mr. Serafimovski says this: "I did not try to find out who was involved in the death of QA, because I was told that a lot of security forces were involved in those events." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page of that statement and focus on paragraph 13. And if you look at the fourth line of that paragraph it says-- it records the following: "Although normally the investigative judge has an obligation to ascertain the cause of the injuries, as I explained earlier, I learned that these persons were injured during the clashes with the Macedonian security forces. It was a war situation and at that time I did not even think about trying to learn the cause of these injuries." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at paragraph 15, Mr. Serafimovski said this: "I have read the autopsy file, and I have seen the pictures of the deceased. I say again there was no reason for me to do any further investigative steps. In a war, I presumed that the authorised security forces were not doing anything illegal." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "I believe that there were armed clashes in which this person died." That's how he concludes. Is that correct, sir, that the position of Mr. Serafimovski appears to be that he failed to investigate the matter based on the fact that his understanding that nothing illegal occurred?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may interject. I apologise for the interference, but I don't believe that this particular witness at this time can speak to the opinions or potential actions of another witness, especially since I don't believe there has been any foundation with respect to whether or not Dr. Jakovski actually even knows who this particular person is, let alone whether or not he could actually speak to this persons's actions or state of mind at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I was simply asking this witness what his understanding of the explanation given by Mr. Serafimovski was. I wasn't asking him to comment on the accuracy or the -- or otherwise of what this person was saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How is the doctor's understanding going to be any better than the understanding of anybody else and especially the understanding of the members of this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Of limited value, Your Honour. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, I would like to ask you now a number of questions about your findings regarding the autopsy of Mr. Qaili. I think you have indicated to my colleague and noted in your dissection protocol that the death of Mr. Qaili appeared to have been the consequence of a traumatic shock. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that the shock you referred to is a general reaction of the organism?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you've pointed out that the shock in question had been caused by a number of what you have qualified as dynamic blunt use of force on to the body. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you able, sir, to date the -- or to put an exact time on to each and every one of the injuries which Mr. Qaili's body had sustained?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the appearance of the injuries, their colouring, I can say that those injuries were recent.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... A time, a time-line on this?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that they correspond with the documentation related to this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you able to say, sir, whether they had all been inflicted on to the body at the same time or whether they could have been inflicted at different period of time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the body, we could find injuries that originate from the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Speak of this same time, it is the general time since he was brought -- from the moment when he incurred the injury to the moment when he was brought to your institute?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you are not able to be more specific than that, in the sense that you are not able to say whether within that time-period the injuries were sustained at a particular hour or at a particular time rather than now -- than another. Is that correct? In other words, the injuries on the body of Mr. Qaili could have been inflicted at different time during that general time-period.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can never precisely say at what time of day a certain injury was inflicted. When talking about finding out the time when the injuries were inflicted, always this refers to days, weeks or years, and not in hours or minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You were asked a number of questions about the injuries sustained by the head and face of Mr. Qaili. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that the head injuries that you identified on the head of Mr. Qaili would not necessarily be deadly, or lethal?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These injuries, according to their character, are serious bodily injuries with a very specific threat to a person's life.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, however, that the bleeding inside the head was too thin for this injury to be lethal?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was bleeding below the heart and the soft membrane of the brain as well as contusions to the brain itself with an additional fracture of the bones in the base of the skull. Without a medical intervention on time, in order to evacuate the haematoma, the subdural one, and without providing of anti-therapy, therapy in order to reduce the swelling of the brain, these injuries represent an acute threat to the person's or patient's life. However, they are not cause -- a usual cause of immediate death from the very moment when they have been inflicted. Some time has to elapse in order for this swelling to develop.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You have also been asked questions about linear injury to the right arm of Mr. Qaili. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were asked by my colleague to describe the sort of object that could have caused those lines and I think I used the adjective long, heard and blunt. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you able to say whether the object in question would have been flat or circular?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Flat. I can explain why do I believe these objects have been flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they were round, then in the middle of the haematoma or the bruise, there should be a lighter coloured zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that correct, Doctor, that a patient who has received -- would not receive appropriate treatment after such a series of hits to the body could suffer increased plain?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These injuries that have been concluded on the deceased Qaili Atulla have caused major pain.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that the major pain which he would have felt could in turn have increased the risk of a deadly shock to the body?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of the reasons for a shock is the feeling of pain.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think you've told my colleague also that you inspected the ribs or the ribcage of Mr. Qaili. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you mentioned that eight of Mr. Qaili's ribs were broken. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would that have caused breathing problems to Mr. Qaili at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With these kind of fractures as being noted for the deceased, I can say that the left lung basically was dysfunctional, because it was impossible to expand the breathing muscles; that is to say, the muscles for breathing could not move because of the broken ribs.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that a condition that the doctor present would have been able to observe?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. If you have an X-ray during a medical examination, this should be noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And without an X-ray, sir, would the doctor have been able to identify the breathing problems of Mr. Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what sort of medical treatment would be appropriate in those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immobilisation, assisted breathing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about infusion, vitamin, antibiotic, analgesic and Tegrelin, would that be appropriate?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The analgetics [as interpreted] only reduce the pain and everything else is suboperative therapy and protection from tetanus.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that would not be sufficient, in other words?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is sub --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction, not suboperative but supporting therapy.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I just repeat my question, doctor. Would a prescription of infusion, vitamin, antibiotic, analgesic and Tegrelin be appropriate or inappropriate considering the condition of Mr. Qaili?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You have indicated a number of injuries which you have perceived on the body of Mr. Qaili at the time. Did you identify any signs of cigarette burns or other burns to the body?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We haven't noted if there were any. I am quite sure that they have been -- would have been noted.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just a question about cause of death. Is that correct that, according to your own regulation and in your own medical documentation, you can only list one cause of death, not concurrent causes of death? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We always provided just one single reason for death, and in the opinion, the last part of the section protocol, there is a description of the way how the death occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps it is a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We need to have the second break now - I think the doctor would probably enjoy that - and we will resume at five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, you remember I asked you a moment ago what treatment would be -- should be prescribed to a person suffering from the sort of injuries which Mr. Qaili had received at his ribcage, and you said assisted breathing. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, assisted breathing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then I asked you about other prescription which consisted of infusion, vitamin, antibiotic, analgesic, and Tegrelin, and then I asked you whether that treatment was appropriate or inappropriate, and you said appropriate. My question to you is this: When you answered my question as to whether the treatment would be appropriate, did you mean those, infusion, vitamin, antibiotic, analgesic, and Tegrelin together with the breathing -- assisted breathing assistance or would the infusion, vitamin, and so on be sufficient in themself, appropriate on their own?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from this therapy, also anti-edematic therapy should be administered in order to reduce the edema on the brain.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And so that we're clear, because my question wasn't -- would an appropriate response to the injuries of Mr. Qaili necessarily include assisted breathing, in your view?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the specific case, I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now a few questions about the injuries which you were shown earlier by my colleague. Is that correct that many of the injuries which you observed on Mr. Qaili's body would have been consistent with what is known as defensive wounds?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The characteristic defensive wounds were not found on the body of Atulla Qaili, but the injuries on the right upper arm and lower arm could be defensive wounds, but they are not the typical, the characteristic defensive wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think you you've said the following in your statement to the Prosecution, and I'll ask you to explain what you mean: "We don't exclude the possibility that they are defence wounds but they are not classical defence wounds." That's at paragraph 25 of your statement. What did you mean to say when you said that they were not classical defensive wounds? What was unclassical about them?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The classical defensive wounds are found in the lower arms in the external side, that means to the say the side where -- where the pinky finger is when a person raises his arm to defend themselves. In that case, you find there bruises, contusions, and in a case of harder force applied, then you -- there are also fractures of the forearm bones.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that based on the findings that you made on to the body of Mr. Qaili you could not exclude the possibility that those injuries that you described were in fact defensive wounds?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we could not be absolutely certain that those are defensive wounds. Rather, they are atypical as defensive wounds go.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. You have also been asked a number of questions about paraffin test and the paraffin glove test. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've indicated, I believe, that the decision to carry out this test was taken by you and Professor Duma. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know if Professor Duma was asked at the time to perform that particular exercise on the body of Mr. Qaili? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was our decision before the autopsy started.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask that the registry bring up Rule 65 ter 1D226. It's 1D002440.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, that is the OTP statement of Professor Duma. It's taken -- was taken on the 5th of February, 2007 and I would like the registry to go to page 8 of that statement. That's 1D002447, and I will read the paragraph to you, as we don't have a Macedonian version of that document. And if you can look at paragraph 37, doctor, it says the following: "At that time we did paraffin tests quite often." Perhaps I'll ask you this: You have indicated from a scientific point of view, the paraffin glove test was not the most reliable, perhaps. Was there other alternative in Macedonia at the time that was more reliable to determine the nature of nitrate and nitrite particles?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time and not even today there is an institution in the Republic of Macedonia which can perform a method more modern than the paraffin test in order to establish the presence of nitrate particles.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Duma, Professor Duma goes on to say this: "As for this particular cases," he's talking about Mr. Qaili, "I do not recall if someone contacted me and spoke to me about the body which would have caused us to do a paraffin test. It is logical that someone called us in this instance, but I cannot say this for certain at this time." Is that consistent with your experience, sir, that when you perform such a test it would generally be either a request or an inquiry from an investigative judge to that effect?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the autopsy, we as experts in forensic medicine, if we believe that it is necessary to perform additional tests in order to establish evidence, material evidence, we then perform those without having received an additional order from an investigating judge, and then we inform the judge about the result, and we enter all the data into the section protocol, and we charge it per price list of the institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, you have answered my next question, which was, the result of any such test is sent to the investigative judge and to no one else. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You also indicated that the problem with a paraffin glove test is that it is capable to identify nitrites and nitrate particles but that it does not really permit a reliable assessment as to the nature, the scientific nature of those particles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would it also be correct to say that an experienced specialist could draw certain conclusions or inferences from the appearance, the number, the intensity, the shape, and the position of these particles on the body of an individual?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is possible. A experienced specialist could draw a conclusion depending on the data they have about the event, but to be certain and know whether that person has used the fire-arm in question, one should conduct tests.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So what you saying, doctor, is that an experienced practitioner would be able to increase, if you want, the probability of those particles coming from a gun but not to the point of absolute certainty. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, because when firing the weapon, the particles, the gunpowder particles are found at particular places on the hand of the person who shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, sir, that the nitrite particles that come from a gun have a particular shape because they have been burned in the process of the shooting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that because of the same process, they are more intense than unburned particles?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Am I correct to understand that a nitrite particle that has burned as a result of the process of shooting from a gun would leave a more intense mark than a particle which would come from another substance containing nitrite?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure with regards to this question. I can't answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You have been shown earlier the section protocol or autopsy report that you prepared with Professor Duma. Am I correct to understand that the result of the examination that you have carried out were sent to the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, once again, the report is not sent to the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only to the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to ask you a question about your experience generally. Is that correct that when an investigative judge learns of the death of an individual who was being investigated, he would seek confirmation to -- from your institute or from another medical institute prior to requesting the withdrawal of the proceedings against that person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What should they request from us?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Whether an investigative judge would sometimes seek from you confirmation of the death of a particular individual who was the subject of criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We issue a death certificate only after we perform the forensic autopsy. Without a forensic autopsy, we could not issue a death certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll help myself making my point clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Exhibit P46. It's ET-0463-8876 - 0463-8877-1 and the Macedonian version is Exhibit P46, 0463-8774-103.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In your binder, sir, it is at tab 18, 1-8.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the record, there's a date that appears on the top left-hand corner of the English version as 03 August 2001. And it seems to come from a stamp in the original version. However, they are two handwritings which Your Honour can identify in the Macedonian version which seem to suggest 309 and 09 further on the right of that document, and that would seem to be consistent with the rest of the document that the date should in fact be 3rd of September, rather than the 3rd of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to draw your attention to the first paragraph. As you can see it's a document, once again, which comes from the investigative Judge Velce Pancevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again it bears the same number on the top right-hand corner, which is KIN 0436-01. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on the first paragraph it says that: "Therefore on 21st August 2001 the court handed down," and then there's a title, "decision, dismissal of investigation against Qaili Atulla. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then in this paragraph it refers to a decision on enforcement of investigation against that person dated 14 August 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And also a decision of detention for a period of 30 days. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it. Could you show it to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. It's --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Then if you go further down into the section with the subheading argument, the second paragraph in that document, Judge Pancevski says the following: "During the investigative procedure it was confirmed that the accused person Qaili Atulla from the village of Ljuboten is deceased." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it says apparently, within the Official Note KI number 436-01 dated 28 August 2001, it is stated that an autopsy was performed and also expert testimony was obtained, that is, a dissection protocol SP number 11918-245-01 dated 14 August 2001 from the Forensic Institute at the medical faculty Skopje. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Protocol, sir, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then Judge Pancevski goes on to say this: "Identification was performed during the investigation which is evident within the Official Note number 351, certified under number 19.5.1-1651 dated 20 August 2001 obtained by MOI of Republic of Macedonia, SOI Skopje forensic department, Skopje." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then he says: "Regarding the fact that during the investigative procedure death of the accused person Atulla Qaili was confirmed, it was decided as in the purview of the decision in accordance to the hereinabove stated and pursuant to Article 135 from ZKP" -- that's that criminal procedure code. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And decision dismissing an investigation against Mr. Qaili was handed down on the 21st of August, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, is that correct that during the crisis period in Macedonia some Albanian citizens boycotted public services, including by refraining from asking for death certificates for their lost relatives. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P149. It's N005-0547-ET. And it has the same ERN number for the Macedonian version and it is it under tab 19 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you look at the top left-hand corner, it's a document that comes from the Ministry of Internal Affairs, sector for internal affairs, Skopje, department for internal affairs, OOR Cair, and it's being -- it's noted motor vehicle inspector submitted by Robertino Acevski, and it names the source, and it is dated 15 August 2001, and it is in the operational information numbered 540. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The subject of this operational information is: Information acquired on civil boycott by the citizen of Albanian nationality on the territory of the department for internal affair, Cair. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the document notes the following: "On 14 August 2001 at around 18 hours at the premises of the department for internal affairs, OOR Cair, a conversation was carried out with Dr. Nada Pesik from the home call service in Cair who informed me that during 2001 they have noticed that citizens of Albanian nationality do not ask the service to issue them certificate -- death certificates for deceased persons. That is, they do not report the deceased, and although they are buried they are still registered with us as alive." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it says: "Namely, since the armed activities started in Tanusevsci until now, citizens of Albanian nationality do not report at all deceased persons, unlike in the period for the past years when there were daily reports by Albanian citizens. According to the doctor's opinion, they buried the deceased at the village cemeteries without the necessary documentation for burial." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, if I may show you now a document that has been admitted earlier as P288. It is under tab 12 of your binder. You recall being showed [sic] that document by my colleague?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is a death certificate for the person, Atulla Qaili. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you issued that document on the 23 of February of 2004?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that's when the family or the relatives of Mr. Qaili asked you for such a certificate?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever they requested it, then they received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as far as you can tell, and as far as you know, there had been no such request from the relatives of Mr. Qaili prior to that time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no prior request.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've pointed out to my colleague that in this same document the death of Mr. Qaili is registered as being violent. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that those findings that you make in these documents are not binding on the investigative judge or on the prosecutor. They can make their own assessment about that matter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document issued to the family so that they are able to complete the necessary formalities to deregister the deceased.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: More generally perhaps, then, when you make findings as to the nature or the cause of a death and that's -- the document is then forwarded on to the investigative judge, is that correct that your own findings are not binding in any way on the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision of the investigating judge is their own, whether they will initiate an investigation or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. I have also asked you a few questions earlier about fingerprints and papillary line, and you've indicated, I believe, that the test was not carried out by you, and you indicated also your understanding that this exercise had occurred at the Butel morgue. Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 226. That is N000-1242-ET.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be N000-1242 in the Macedonian, and that is under tab 21 of your binder, sir. If can you look at the top again, top left corner of that document. It says that it comes from the Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior, forensic investigation administration. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and on the top right-hand corner there is a number, 19.5.1. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says: Record of the evidence and object found at the site." And it says: "On 17 August 2001," the time is not mentioned. It says in: Butel chapel -- "At Butel chapel an on-site investigation was carried out into the crime of unidentified male body. The following took part in an on-site investigation team." And then there's a first name, Nikolov, with actual and illegible last name. And it refers to fingerprint of the right index finger. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that, sir, is, again, consistent with what you've said earlier about the fingerprint test and papillary line. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if I could --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D68, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If this witness may be shown Rule 65 ter -- it's Prosecution Rule 65 ter 110 with an ERN N000-1253-ET. The Macedonian version would be N001-1253.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Doctor, it is under tab 22 of your binder. If I may ask you to look at the top left-hand corner. It says: "Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Internal Affairs, sector for internal affairs of the city of Skopje, criminal technique department." And, again, it has this number, 19.5.1, 1651, and it is submitted by Zlatko Dosevski on the 20th of August, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is it submitted to the SVR, sector for internal affair, OKT, criminal techniques department. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is an Official Note numbered 357 [sic] about the identification of NN - that's unknown person - deceased person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the transcript has recorded me, or I have misspoke, and has number 357. It should have been Official Note number 351.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Drawing your attention to the first paragraph, Doctor, where it says: "On 17 August 2001 by the inspection team of SVR Skopje, criminal techniques department, fingerprints are taken of papillary lines of NN deceased persons in the chapel, Butel, Skopje, with the aim to determine the identity of the same." Would you agree that it is consistent with the previous document that I have shown you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then the next paragraph says: "On the same day, the search inspectorate at SVR Skopje brought in a file card for issuing a personal identification card in the name of Qaili Atulla, from father Avdi, mother Hava, born 3rd November 1965 in the village Ljuboten," then there's a number, "in order to compare the fingerprint left on the file card for issuing a personal identification card with a fingerprint taken from the unknown person." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then it concludes: "After conducting a comparison, it was concluded that the fingerprints of the papillary lines are identical." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'd wish to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D69 Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown -- it's again a Prosecution Rule 65 ter document, 108. It is ERN N000-1246-DT.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, it is under tab 23 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And for the registry, the ERN in Macedonian is N000-1246.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As you can see from the top left-hand corner, it's again a document from the Basic Court Skopje II, Skopje, from the investigation department with the same number, 436-01. It is dated 22nd of August and it is send to the KPU prison Skopje, Skopje. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it has a header saying: Subject, information, connection KI number 436-01 dated 14 August 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if I may draw your attention to the second paragraph in that document, it records the following: "Because of existing of suspicion that the person Qaili Atulla, father's name Avdi, mother's Hava, born on 5 November 1965 in Skopje, last address Ljuboten village, citizen of Republic of Macedonia, has died, identification of a body was conducted ..." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it says in the next paragraph: "The crime techniques department of the Skopje city sector of the Ministry of Interior, within MVR has confirmed that the unidentified dead person is actually Qaili Atulla." Then it cites the father's name, the mother's name, and the ID number. Could you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says that the conclusion was confirmed with comparing the fingerprints of the dead body with the fingerprints taken from issuing an identification card. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is, again, signed by Mr. Pancevski, Judge Pancevski. Is that correct, sir, it is signed by Mr. Pancevski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... realised that the translation I have in my hand mentions the date of birth of Mr. Qaili as being once 5 of November and 3rd of November, which seems to be a problem in the original as well. And we would wish to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D70, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to ask you a few more questions now related to a different subject which relate to the period of time of August of 2001. Is that correct that on the 12 of August of 2001 you received information that a number of individuals had been killed in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that day, I was on duty, and by the investigating judge, Ognen Stavrev, I was informed that several persons had died and that I might be called to go on site to make an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that the team which was formed on that occasion included not only yourself and Judge Stavrev but also Deputy Prosecutor Milan Galevski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it also included a number of technicians from the crime technique police, as it is known?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those crime technicians, sir, they are employees of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also that such an on-site visit is -- or the team which takes part in such an on-site visit is being lead and is under the authority of the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that all information collected in the connection of such an on-site investigation is sent to him and no other member of the team. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the information collected by the investigating team are submitted to the investigation judge and no nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Prosecution Rule 65 ter 103 with an ERN N000-7352-ET-09. And the Macedonian version is N000-7352, and it is at tab 26 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Doctor, I will come back on the specifics of your activities during that day and the following days as far as they concern Ljuboten. But do you recognise this document as the report which you prepared after your taking part in the attempted on-site investigation in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the report that I prepared for the public prosecutor Stavre Dzikov upon the request of my director.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That was my next question again. Is that correct from the indication that is on the top of this document that it was sent to the public prosecutor Mr. Dzikov, and that you had made a request to that effect. You have now indicated that Professor Duma had made the same request. Is that how it should be understood: Both of them had requested you to do that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Professor Duma conveyed to me that I'm supposed to submit a written information to Stavre Dzikov related to the event when I was on duty in the following days as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll now ask you to look at the first sentence of that document. I will read it out to you in the English. It says that: "On 12 August 2001 at 18 hours we were informed by the investigative judge Ognen Stavrev from the Basic Court Skopje I that we should go on a site investigation in Ljuboten Village where were situated five dead bodies of Albanian terrorists." I'll just stop there for a minute. Is that correct that at the time when you received the information from Judge Stavrev, he had indicated to you that the five dead bodies were in fact the bodies of terrorists?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you report goes on to say this: "That's why the whole team that was on duty in the Forensic Institute and criminology were called to come to the their places of duty." Is that how it happened?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it says: "At 1930 we were informed by the crime technique of Ministry of Interior that were on the spot that the military activities are still going on. There is -- so it was not safe to go and perform the site investigation." Is that information which you received at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The investigating judge called me again at 1930 and told me that we couldn't go on the site because it was unsafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So am I correct to understand that both the crime technique of the MOI and Judge Stavrev called you later that day, to give you that information, that it was unsafe to go?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only the investigating judge, Ognen Stavrev, and he had gotten the information from the crime techniques.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when Judge Stavrev referred to Albanian terrorists, did he refer in fact to members of the National Liberation Army. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what he thought and this is what I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you inform Professor Duma on that day about your conversation with Judge Stavrev?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the very moment when the -- when I had the first phone call at 6.00 p.m., this is the moment when I informed Professor Duma.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that you were called again by Judge Stavrev two or three days later?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall now whether it was two or three days after the first phone call from Judge Stavrev, or is it too far away now to recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was two to three days later. But since I have the document before me I believe this is true, what is written there, because the memory was very fresh at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll show you number of documents later which may help you in that regard. But I would like to focus at this stage on the second paragraph in this document where you said this: "Three days later on 15 August 2001, at 1430, we were informed by the investigative judge, Ognen Stavrev, from the Basic Court Skopje I that site investigation will take place in Ljuboten village regarding the dead bodies of Albanian terrorists that were found there, because the situation on the terrain has calmed down." Is that correct? Is that what Judge Stavrev told you at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say this: "From the Forensic Institute and criminology, the duty doctor headed towards the police station in Butel where the following persons were present: The investigative judge from the Basic Court Skopje I, Ognen Stavrev; the deputy public prosecutor, Milan Galevski and the team of the Ministry of Interior, NVR, crime technique sector. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you recorded a meeting. During the meeting with the head of the police station Bute, we were informed that in the village there are still terrorist groups who are not allowing site investigation to take place and are not handing over the dead bodies of the terrorists for identification and autopsy." Is that what you were told at the time by the head of the police station Butel?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall what the name of that person was or is?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you also told that there might still be NLA members in the village at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did the head of the police station also warn you that you could be kidnapped or fired upon if you tried to enter the village?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he offered us, in case we decided to go, a transporter, helmets, and flakjackets.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also underline the fact that he could not guarantee your safety; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this is the reason why the investigating judge and the public prosecutor decided for us not to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the decision whether to go or not to go was the decision of the investigative judge and the investigative judge only; is that correct? He was the one to decide where you should or shouldn't go in the village.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Him and the deputy public prosecutor Milan Galevski, they both said that in such circumstances when the security is not guaranteed of the investigating team, then we should not go to the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So upon that decision having been made is that correct that the entire team returned to Skopje?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And a few hours you were called again by Judge Stavrev about the same matter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you again to focus on your report, the next paragraph and I'll read it out to you. "The same day, a few hours later, between 1630 and 1700 hours we were called again by the investigative judge, Ognen Stavrev, from the Basic Court Skopje I to go on site investigation in Ljuboten village because he had received information that the situation on the terrain is safe and it is possible to conduct site investigation." Do you recall receiving that information?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that upon receiving that information the same group of people, Judge Stavrev, deputy public prosecutor Galevski, yourself and a member of the crime technique all went back to Cair or Butel police station?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that upon your arrival you were told once again by the head of the Butel police station that it wouldn't be safe for you and your team to go into the village?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And sometime later you were also received some information from the head of the police station Butel that the bodies had been buried. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, once again, the judge ordered the entire team to go back to Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'd like to tendered this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D71, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, once you had prepared this report, did you discuss it at all with Professor Duma?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just gave it to Professor Duma which was then archived and the -- then it was sent to the addressee.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So a copy was sent by yourself or by Professor Duma to the Public Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It goes through our secretary, as it usually does.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you didn't send a copy to the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not. It was requested by Stavre Dzikov not by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the witness may be shown Exhibit P99. It's N000-0162 in the English. It is under tab 27, and the Macedonian version is N000-0599.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If can you look at the top left-hand corner doctor. It says: "Republic of Macedonia, Public Prosecution Office of the Republic of Macedonia," then it has a number 231-01. It's dated 18 November 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the title of that document is information on the events happened in the area of the village Ljuboten, Skopje, in the period August 10, 11, 12 and the 14th, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll ask the registry to go on to the third page of that document. That's N000-164. In doctor that is also the third page in the Macedonian version. And is that correct that this document is being signed by the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia Stavre Dzikov?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you turn to the next page of that document, that would be N00 -- yes, thank you. And sir, do you recognise your report which I've just read out to you with a slightly different translation into the English. But in the Macedonian, is that the same document that I have just shown to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO JAKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document that I wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would. I'm afraid, Doctor, the day has come to an end again, so we must adjourn and continue tomorrow at 2.15. I remind counsel that we will have two sessions only tomorrow afternoon, finishing by 6.00 p.m. with one break. We now adjourn until 2.15
